title: Equivalence of explicit covariant corepresented infinity functors
statement: Use quasicategories, equivalence edges and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the infinity category of spaces and explicit covariant corepresented functors of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $\mathcal C$; form its functor categories in a larger universe. For a vertex $c$, write $h_c:\mathcal C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ for precisely the functor obtained from $A=\mathfrak C[\mathcal C]$ by the enriched functor $x\mapsto\operatorname{Sing}|A(c,x)|$ and the rigidification unit, as in that definition. Let $e:g\to a$ be an equivalence edge of $\mathcal C$. Precomposition with the vertex of $A(g,a)$ specified by $e$ induces a coherent natural equivalence $e^*:h_a\xrightarrow{\sim}h_g$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Its component at $x$ is the map $\operatorname{Sing}|A(a,x)|\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(g,x)|$ induced by enriched composition with that vertex. If $e':a\to g$ is an inverse equivalence edge, precomposition with $e'$ gives an inverse natural equivalence. The assertions concern the full Kan mapping complexes and all naturality coherences, not only their sets of components. No colimit or accessibility hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ is required.

source.place: Section 5.1.3, opening construction on printed pp. 319-320 (rigidification followed by Sing-realization enriched Hom), applied covariantly with the first object fixed; Section 1.2.3 (homotopy category) and Proposition 1.2.4.1 (equivalences). Supporting explicit composition compatibility: Kerodon Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF), especially Propositions 4.6.8.11-4.6.8.12 and 4.6.8.19. Statement extracted from the retained argument in step 5 of lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $P:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ equal to the explicit singular-realization Hom pairing of [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda], with $D=\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal U=\mathcal V$. Transpose the second variable to obtain $T:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Its restriction at a constant first vertex $c$ is exactly $h_c$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]: every first-variable subset path maps to an identity, so the formula is precisely $H_c$ followed by the rigidification unit. The reversed edge $e^{\mathrm{op}}:a\to g$ therefore gives an edge $T(e^{\mathrm{op}}):h_a\to h_g$. At $x$ the pairing formula is precomposition with the specified vertex $e\in A(g,a)_0$. Associativity makes it commute with postcomposition by every enriched morphism, and the pairing definition supplies compatibility with every simplicial operator. Thus this is the required coherent transformation, with its exact component maps.

source.place: Section 5.1.3, opening construction on printed pp. 319–320; explicit simplexwise Hom pairing of def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda. The inverse-triangle argument below is an elementary expansion of this construction.

proof.text: Choose the stipulated inverse edge $e':a\to g$ and both inverse triangles in $\mathcal C$, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Reversing their vertex order gives triangles in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ with edge triples $(e^{\mathrm{op}},e'^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{id}_a)$ and $(e'^{\mathrm{op}},e^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{id}_g)$. Applying the simplicial map $T$ to these actual $2$-simplices gives $2$-simplices in the functor simplicial set with edge triples $(e^*,e'^*,\operatorname{id}_{h_a})$ and $(e'^*,e^*,\operatorname{id}_{h_g})$. Here $e'^*=T(e'^{\mathrm{op}})$ has, by the same pairing formula, precisely precomposition with $e'$ as its component at $x$. Simplicial maps preserve faces and degeneracies, so the long edges are the specified identity transformations. These are coherent inverse-triangle witnesses, not an identification with right-pinched composition.

source.place: Section 5.1.3, opening construction on printed pp. 319–320; explicit simplexwise Hom pairing of def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda. The inverse-triangle argument below is an elementary expansion of this construction.

proof.text: Evaluation at each vertex $x$ is a simplicial map by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It carries the two triangles just constructed to triangles in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ with edges $(e_x^*,e'_x^*,\operatorname{id}_{h_a(x)})$ and $(e'_x^*,e_x^*,\operatorname{id}_{h_g(x)})$. Hence $e_x^*$ is an equivalence edge with inverse $e'_x^*$ by the definition of equivalence. The objects here are exactly the full Kan complexes $\operatorname{Sing}|A(a,x)|$ and $\operatorname{Sing}|A(g,x)|$, not their component sets. No comparison with another mapping-space model or weak-equivalence detection theorem is used.

source.place: Section 5.1.3, opening construction on printed pp. 319–320; explicit simplexwise Hom pairing of def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda. The inverse-triangle argument below is an elementary expansion of this construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with indexing simplicial set $\mathcal C$ and target quasicategory $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ to the edge $e^*$ constructed in Step 1. Step 3 verifies its hypothesis at every vertex, so $e^*$ is a coherent natural equivalence. Step 2 supplies the inverse $e'^*$ and both inverse triangles for this very transformation; Step 1 identifies every component with the required precomposition map. All functor categories are formed in the containing universe as stipulated. Only smallness, the given equivalence edge and its inverse witnesses were used; no colimit or accessibility hypothesis was introduced.
